title: HC Mike LaFleur Postgame Press Conference | Week 10 vs. Los Angeles Rams
headline: Offense collapsed in a Week 10 loss to the Rams, and Trey McBride is being doubled on nearly every third down, a problem the coach expects to last the rest of the season.
summary: LaFleur said the only injury was Jordan Burch's knee, which will be tested Monday, and he would not call it good or bad yet. He defended first-time starting QB Carson, saying he did everything asked and was hurt by a pick right before halftime, a second pick on a misrun route by a back, and a fourth-down snap-count error. The offense had only about 34 snaps, went 0-for-6 on third down, ran for 34 yards and struggled against a strong Rams front, and LaFleur called the roster battered. He said Trey McBride is doubled on basically all third downs and that this will continue for the next seven weeks. He praised Simi Fehoko's catch on a deep throw. The defense gave up 46 carries for 202 yards and got burned by play-action. LaFleur framed the last seven weeks as a major evaluation of the roster, with injuries giving other players a chance to step up, and he said Michael Wilson was not in the lineup.

injuries.detail: Knee injury in the game. Tests Monday, and LaFleur would not say whether it is good or bad until then.
LaFleur said "Mike's not in there," meaning he did not play. No reason or timeline was given.

signals.claim: Defenses will keep double-teaming McBride on basically all third downs for the next seven weeks.
signals.note: Constant double coverage on third downs limits his upside, especially with a first-time starting QB and a depleted receiver group.
signals.quote: they just double trey on, on basically all third downs

signals.note: The coach singled out a deep throw to him as excellent, so he may be a rising target in a thin receiver room.
signals.quote: I thought the dagger that he threw to Simi was an excellent throw.

signals.note: Defensive depth is a concern, and his availability for next week is unknown.
signals.quote: Not gonna even say if it's good or bad until I know more tomorrow.

topics.detail: LaFleur said Carson did everything asked, delivered intermediate throws well and looked sturdy. He blamed the two interceptions and the fourth-down failure on teammates' errors. Carson is not on the provided roster, so no signal is attributed to him.
About 34 offensive snaps, 0-for-6 on third down and 34 rushing yards against a top front. LaFleur said the team is banged up and called the result shared accountability.
The Rams ran 46 times for 202 yards and also beat the defense with play-action. LaFleur said the defense has to find a way to get off the field.
The final seven weeks are a roster evaluation with a focus on continuity. LaFleur said injuries open opportunities for new players and compared the situation to Michael Wilson's breakout last year.

title: HC Mike LaFleur Press Conference: November 16, 2026
headline: Carson Beck got a positive review after his debut and may start again, while Trey McBride is likely to keep drawing double coverage. Jordan Burch is out for the season.

LaFleur put the sack before halftime on himself for the play call and said the other sacks came from protection losing too quickly. He said the offense has to turn plays like the missed pylon-route shot into touchdowns, and that the line and receivers must do more to help the quarterback. On Trey McBride, he said the offense can move him around on early downs, but opponents will bracket or double him on third down, so other pass catchers need to step up. An unnamed player with an ankle injury is 'trending well', with an update due Wednesday and a chance he starts this week. LaFleur also hopes to get a few offensive linemen back this week and wants to build continuity over the final seven weeks.

title: Head Coach Kevin Stefanski on Falcons' Week 10 matchup vs. Chiefs | Press Conference
headline: Falcons come off a poor loss to the Chiefs and head into the bye with offensive process under review; Drake London cleared from his concussion check, and Corey Levin and DeMarcco Hellams got their first starts of the season.
summary: Stefanski called the loss to the Chiefs frustrating and disappointing. He said the team will own it, learn from it and use the bye week for a deeper self-scout. He repeatedly said the coaches need to give players a better plan and that the players then need to execute it. That includes reviewing the play-calling process, the practice plan and the run game, which has been outrushed in five of the last six weeks. He said the screen game has not delivered since some good moments a few weeks ago, and that a good offense needs an efficient and explosive pass game to help the run. Players are in the building Monday and Tuesday, then off until next Monday. Avieon Terrell was a healthy scratch because of special-teams numbers, though Stefanski called him an important part of the team now and in the future after the C.J. Henderson extension. Corey Levin and DeMarcco Hellams were praised for their first starts of the year. Drake London left late with a concussion evaluation and has been cleared. Asked about evaluating the quarterback with a struggling offense around him, Stefanski said evaluations are weekly and take circumstances into account, but that everyone has to be better.

title: Joe Brady On Rookie Development, Room To Improve, And More
headline: Bills' offense leaned on James Cook (18 carries, 74-yard outside zone TD) while managing his workload. Amani Hooker played every defensive snap in his first game, and Christian Benford's availability is a day-to-day question.
summary: Brady was very positive on Amani Hooker, who played 100% of the snaps. The staff set no snap target and let him play as much as he could handle. Hooker picked up the defense quickly, and the coach says he will keep learning it week to week. Brady waved off the idea that the defensive turnaround came only against backup quarterbacks, crediting the game plans and communication. He was blunt about the pre-snap penalties (illegal shifts, offsides, special teams), calling them embarrassing and drive-killing. He defended the offense's starts, saying third downs were the issue and that first and second down were fine, and he expects second-half adjustments to pay off. On Christian Benford, who has not finished two straight games, he said the team will go day by day. Players like Spencer Brown may skip practice but play if they can. He said James Cook's workload is monitored, with 18 carries yesterday after two straight 80-plus-play games, and that Cook's 74-yard touchdown came from a change-up outside zone after earlier calls were checked out of. He also credited the conditioning emphasis for wearing teams down, said he does not chase average depth of target, and blamed his own sideline handling, not Josh Allen's read, for his frustration around the deep interception.

title: Dave Canales on the first place Panthers, playoff hunger and the week ahead
headline: Canales loved the film: Chuba Hubbard had a big day and the rookie safety Wheatley passed Nick Scott for snaps. T-Mac and Coker have been quiet, and he offered no concrete fix beyond formations and motions.

His main complaint was penalties, both pre-snap and post-snap, especially personal fouls after the whistle. He said repeat offenders could lose playing time, but he wouldn't commit to that. On the quiet stretch for Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker, he credited opposing secondaries and said the offense is trying formations and motions to get them access. He also noted that attention on them is opening things up for Darren Waller, Hubbard and the tight ends. Rookie safety Zakee Wheatley played every snap while Nick Scott was in a lesser role, after the two talked it through. Canales credited the improved run defense to all 11 players rallying to the ball and to better info on formations and personnel from the new defensive coordinator. He declined to give injury updates, said Xavier Legette (two snaps in his return) will help 'when it's time', and said Devin Lloyd came through fine as far as he knew.

title: Zac Taylor Speaks to Media Following White Bengal Win Over Steelers | PRESS CONFERENCE
headline: Burrow and Ja'Marr Chase are locked in during a 38-18 win over Pittsburgh, and the pass-heavy offense (24 passes to 6 runs at one point) should continue Monday night at Washington, while Dalton Risner's knee is a minor concern.
summary: Zac Taylor was pleased with the 38-18 divisional win over the Steelers, which moved Cincinnati to 7-2 with control of its own playoff fate. He said all three phases set the tone early. He praised Joe Burrow's accuracy, patience and downfield vision, and credited an offensive line that has protected so well it lets the team throw freely. He singled out Ja'Marr Chase for tremendous catches and for an extra gear that tracks down deep balls. Dohnte Meyers scored his first NFL touchdown at the end of the first half, and Taylor spoke warmly about his long road to get there. The defense hurried Aaron Rodgers, tackled well on the perimeter and covered well downfield, which made Pittsburgh one-dimensional. On injuries, Taylor said a knee issue for a player the captions render as "Riser" (almost certainly guard Dalton Risner) doesn't seem too serious, but the player couldn't finish the game. Taylor warned that the league is humbling and said the focus now turns to Monday night in Washington.

title: Brian Schottenheimer: Postgame Week 10 #SFvsDAL
headline: Cowboys lost 46-40 to the 49ers after the defense collapsed in the second half. Tyler Booker and DaRon Bland both have ankle injuries, with imaging pending, while George Pickens returned and looked strong.
summary: Schottenheimer called the second-half defense unacceptable. He blamed poor tackling and three explosive touchdown plays of 65+ yards, and said Dallas had led 17-16 at halftime. He wouldn't commit to a verdict on coordinator Christian Parker and said the staff will study the film. He explained that a cover-zero all-out blitz left Von Miller isolated on Christian McCaffrey for the final touchdown, and said Parker went with a call he liked that didn't work. He pointed to missed tackles, tackling too high, and poor eye discipline against reverses and naked boots, and said effort wasn't the problem. On offense, he praised Dak Prescott's competitiveness and was happy to have George Pickens back, saying Pickens is a playmaker once the ball is in his hands. Tyler Booker and DaRon Bland both have ankle injuries, and the severity will depend on X-rays and MRIs. KaVontae Turpin gutted it out, and Dallas limited his kick-return work because of the physical hits while keeping him on punt returns and offense. The team returns home next week.

He added that the two will always give Dallas a chance to win, though he admitted the team needs better discipline after Pickens' taunting penalty. Dak Prescott threw 51 times in the two-minute mode and was sacked once, which the coach credited to the protection and Dak's competitiveness. Tyler Booker and DaRon Bland (a different ankle from before) could both miss time, and T.J. Bass is the next man up. Jalen Thompson is trending better but will be checked after a light workout, and P.J. Locke will likely miss another week with back-to-back concussions. The coach also said the run game needs to improve and that explosive plays are down this year.

title: HC Sean Payton on Denver’s focus following the bye week: ‘The improvement in certain areas’
headline: Payton says the Broncos' run game needs better blocking after a so-so Carolina game, and he downplays any offensive line shake-up or more inside linebacker snaps for backups.
summary: Coming off the bye, Payton said the team just held a meeting on improving in specific areas for the second half of the season. His main offensive point was that Denver has to block better and be in the right place, because he graded the run game as average against Carolina and wants more consistency. Defensively, he pointed to third-and-long and fourth-and-long situations, which he called an Achilles heel last year that resurfaced recently. Asked about his Colin Cowherd interview and the offensive line, he said the interview isn't tied to any line changes. He said the staff is evaluating every part of the offense and will spend a lot of time on mid-season cut-ups covering scheme and personnel. On inside linebacker depth, he pushed back on the idea of lightening the starters' load: the starters will play, and backups only get snaps if they earn them. He also declined to give specifics on a trade that fell through and said there was no loophole in the trade process. Finally, he briefly covered how the team handled the Friday air travel disruption, saying staff checked on players who were out of town and about three were still finalizing plans.

title: Matt LaFleur reflects on loss to Vikings while looking ahead to upcoming matchup with Rams
headline: Packers' pass protection collapsed against Minnesota, and LaFleur is publicly sticking with his OL coach. Kevin Zeitler (ankle) and Sean Rhyan (ankle) are the line's key returns for the Rams after the bye, and Skyy Moore is the one to watch.
summary: LaFleur called the pass protection against the Vikings pretty bad, citing scheme problems, lost one-on-ones, and missed chip blocks. He put the first blame on himself and his play calling, and wished he had called more quick-game, ball-out-fast plays. He is staying with the offensive line coach, saying the blame belongs to everyone. He said Minnesota jumped the cadence, and that the Packers' own late play clocks and lack of motion made it worse. Early turnovers, a red-zone pick and a missed field goal put them down 20-0, which forced them into the pass-heavy game Minnesota wants. Kevin Zeitler was expected to start but hurt his ankle in practice, and the staff wouldn't let him play despite his push. LaFleur hopes to have Micah back against the Rams, though a couple of hurdles remain. Kaleb Johnson drew praise for his running and for a blitz pickup. Skyy Moore may not be cleared until late in the week, and the team gets four straight days off before returning Friday.

On Daniel Jones, the coach stressed that he must take care of the football better, but he spread the blame across protection, play calling and other factors, including himself. He made clear Jones remains the leader of the offense. The pass-catching group keeps shifting, with Anthony Gould getting a ton of reps alongside Laquon Treadwell, Nick Westbrook-Ikhine and Ashton Dulin. A calf injury to an unnamed player (the third time on the same leg) has no IR plan yet. Bernhard Raimann's concussion status is also uncertain. CJ Allen was praised for his growing role and communication on the back end. Steichen called Texans receivers Nico Collins and Tank Dell a big challenge and said the defense must prevent explosive plays.

title: Sean McVay, Matthew Stafford & Blake Corum reflect on strong team performance in Sunday’s 34-6 Week 10 win over the Cardinals
headline: Blake Corum is hitting his stride as the Rams' run game becomes the identity, with Kyren Williams paired alongside him in new 20 personnel looks. The offensive line and tight ends are badly banged up heading into the bye.

Eight linemen were needed, with David Quessenberry even used as a tight end. title: Klint Kubiak's takeaways from Fernando Mendoza’s first start, provides injury update on Brock Bowers
headline: Brock Bowers has a significant ankle injury and is day to day with no clear timeline, while rookie QB Fernando Mendoza drew praise after his first start.
summary: Kubiak said Brock Bowers' ankle injury is not as bad as first feared but is still significant. Bowers is day to day, and Kubiak would not say whether he can play this week. He said the offense suffered from losing one of its best players. Fernando Mendoza showed poise and playmaking in his first start, and Kubiak liked his pre-snap operation, checks and preparation. The coaching points were to stay a passer first, protect himself as a runner, and get rid of the ball faster after taking too many hits and sacks. Kubiak spread the blame for the protection problems across the whole offense: getting open, play calling and pass blocking. The run game was good in the first half but disappeared in the second, and a string of early-down failures pushed the offense into drop-back situations. Defensively, two broken plays totaling 105 yards led to 14 points, which Kubiak blamed on effort. He still said he will count on Eric Stokes and praised Maxx Crosby's effort. He also admitted he should have gotten Tre Tucker more involved, and he said he is happy with Trey Zuhn at left guard. A long discussion with the officials after a late kickoff led him to decline a rekick.

headline: Brock Bowers left with an ankle injury and will be reevaluated Monday. The offense fell apart without him, and Kubiak says Fernando Mendoza's mobility should be used more.
summary: Kubiak opened by saying Brock Bowers has an ankle injury and will be reevaluated tomorrow. He didn't know how serious it is, only that it's an ankle. He said the offense's production changed noticeably once Bowers went out, and he blamed himself for not spreading the ball around better. Fernando Mendoza's first start got a positive overall review: he started well, was well prepared, and showed poise, maturity and leadership. Kubiak admitted the staff should have kept rolling Mendoza out in the second half after it worked in the first, and said his mobility gives the offense a different dimension. The offense was poor after halftime, including a three-and-out on the opening second-half drive. Seattle's pressure, including DB blitzes and off-schedule plays, led to six sacks, and the run game averaged under three yards per carry. Kubiak put much of that on himself and the staff. He said the defense took a step forward and kept the team in the game. Seattle's shell coverage also took away the deep ball.

He liked McCord's composure and resiliency in his first outing, especially after Indianapolis scored on defense coming out of halftime and Miami fought back. He said the late sack on third down came from a missed blitz pickup, not the play call. He defended going for it on fourth down in the first half, saying he wanted to be aggressive and had nothing to do with the kicker, and he called the throw to Greg Dulcich a good one before it was tipped. Zeek Biggers hurt his leg and Jordan Phillips hurt his arm, which left Miami with two healthy defensive tackles, and he will know more tomorrow. He did not yet know whether Malik will need surgery. He praised the young defensive backs, including a big play by Michael Taaffe, and was especially proud of rookie Chris Johnson, who scored on a long return and whom he expects to have a very good career. title: Kevin O’Connell on Vikings Fans Support in Green Bay, Jordan Addison’s Injury & Trust with Kirk Cousins

title: Head Coach Mike Vrabel 11/16: "We can't let one play affect the next one"
headline: Drake Maye is unlikely to be available coming out of the bye after a reported ankle fracture. Tommy DeVito is the expected fill-in, and Vrabel says he sees no need to bring in outside QB help.
summary: Vrabel opened by declining to comment on Drake Maye's status, even though multiple reports say he may have a fractured ankle and could miss the rest of the season. Maye was still traveling back to New England and the medical staff needed to reevaluate him. Vrabel said he wouldn't imagine Maye being available coming out of the bye. Most of the session was about the lopsided loss to the Lions, which Vrabel blamed on turnovers, explosive plays allowed, an inefficient run game, and the lack of special teams plays. He said Detroit outplayed and outcoached New England and played harder. He rejected the idea of a locker room problem or lack of trust, calling it frustration after losses at 5-5. He pushed back on Milton Williams' comment that the field contributed to Maye's injury, saying the turf was the same for both teams. On Tommy DeVito, he said the performance wasn't good enough, partly because DeVito had little live action since training camp. He still expects DeVito to be ready after the bye and has a lot of confidence in him. He doesn't currently see a need to add a quarterback, though the staff will discuss it, and he said the backup behind DeVito is improving and would be ready if needed.

title: Aaron Glenn Press Conference (11/16) | Week 11
headline: Geno Smith is still the Jets' starter if healthy, but he is getting imaging on an injury from the game. Cade Klubnik is the next man up if Geno can't go.

title: WATCH: McCarthy on the loss to the Bengals

He said Pittsburgh needed to answer with running hits on the ball. On offense, he pointed to a penalty on a screen and a failure to get going on first down on the road. title: Head Coach Mike Macdonald: "I'm Really Proud Of Our Team"
headline: Seahawks beat the Raiders and head into the bye with Abraham Lucas (ankle) and George Holani (knee) hurt, Sam Darnold's return unclear, and Drew Lock still the starter at 4-0.
summary: Macdonald was proud of the team after a win that he said showed progress in the run game, even though Las Vegas had the better plan in the first half. He praised Drew Lock's scramble touchdowns but wants the two turnovers cleaned up, along with red zone finishing. Abraham Lucas (ankle) and George Holani (knee) both left hurt, and the coach said he doesn't know how severe either injury is. Sam Darnold's status will be clearer after the bye, and he will need a significant amount of practice time before he can play. Jaxon Smith-Njigba was highlighted for making plays in every phase of the offense. Dante Fowler is getting more pass-rush chances now that games are producing passing situations, and Josh Jobe was praised for his tackling. Bobby Hart filled in for Lucas and played well, but Macdonald wouldn't commit to a plan for the offensive line if Lucas misses time. Players are off this week and return next Monday.

summary: Macdonald is optimistic Darnold (ribs) will get a full week of practice next week and play against San Francisco, though he said Darnold couldn't do that right now and some hurdles remain. He confirmed Darnold is the starting QB when healthy. He praised the team's resolve, toughness and connectedness, but said the team needs to stack plays more consistently across all three phases and start games faster. The defensive line has covered for Leonard Williams' absence, with Byron Murphy II praised as a rare three-down, A-gap player who has led the team in sacks. DeMarcus Lawrence has also played well, and Macdonald wants Murphy to keep it going once Williams returns. Abraham Lucas has a sprained ankle with no high/low designation yet, and Holani also got hurt with no update. Quenton Nelson is out and Macdonald wouldn't project his practice status for next week. title: Kyle Shanahan Reacts to Win Over Cowboys, Praises Kaelon Black
headline: Kaelon Black's long TD run earned him more work behind Christian McCaffrey, while Renardo Green left with a back injury and didn't return.
summary: Shanahan said Renardo Green's back was the only injury from the win over Dallas; Green left in the second half and didn't return. He praised the offense's big plays: McCaffrey's 74-yard TD (a blitz pickup that turned into an off-schedule throw from Brock Purdy), the late 66-yard TD with McCaffrey running a route against a defensive end, and Deebo Samuel's 70-yard reverse TD. He said the offense wasn't clean, with penalties, protection issues and a slow first half on the ground. Kaelon Black's big touchdown run got the staff to give him more work afterward, and McCaffrey then returned with a big third-down catch and several large runs. Purdy took five sacks and many hits but never told Shanahan he was hurt. Shanahan said the defense struggled to cover Dallas's receivers, didn't pressure enough and seemed gassed late. He credited Green and the player he called "Demo" (likely Deommodore Lenoir) for playing after missing a full week of practice. He was also pleased with the new receiver Keenan Allen in his first game, a week after arriving. Black's late fumble, a strip by Dallas's No. 92, was recovered, and Shanahan wants to review his ball security on film.

title: Robert Saleh Press Conference | Tennessee Titans
headline: Cam Ward has been handed more control of the offense since the Indy game and Saleh says he is playing much better; Carnell Tate is hoped back this week, while Calvin Ridley (4 snaps) needs more involvement.
summary: Saleh opened by saying several players are still being evaluated from yesterday's injuries, and that the team is hopeful to get Carnell Tate, Anthony Hill, Cody Barton and Fernando Carmona back. Defensively he said the issue in a 40-point loss was third-down playmaking and technique. He pointed to Joshua Williams' coverage busts, a circus catch against Alontae Taylor, and a safety who tucked in too far on a touchdown. He praised Cedric Gray, who helped fill in at linebacker, shared the play-calling duties and made game-saving plays in coverage. He explained that after the Indianapolis game the staff shifted the offensive philosophy to make Cam Ward a field general at the line. He said Ward is more comfortable, faster through progressions and playing in rhythm, though he still needs to cut down on risky throws across his body. Saleh defended John Franklin-Myers' empty stat line, saying the tape shows impact plays and that his back is improving. He said the Marcus Harris benching at corner was his own rotation call, and that Taylor is still adjusting to a bigger outside role after playing nickel at an All-Pro level. He admitted Calvin Ridley's four snaps are a problem the offense needs to fix. He also covered no-huddle tempo variation, converting third-and-longs, and a pick-play call he thought was bad officiating.

title: HC Dan Quinn | 11/17/26
headline: Jacory Croskey-Merritt is 'trending in the right area' toward a 21-day window return, with the decision due this week. Ben Sinnott had his best game as a Commander, and Quinn wants more downfield shots for Jayden Daniels.
summary: Quinn opened by praising the complementary football in the Giants win, especially the fourth-quarter sequence of defensive stops and a two-minute touchdown drive. He said the team has been in about six close games in the first half and wants that margin to improve in the 'second season.' He expects the defense to keep improving in communication, disguises and tackling, but says it still gives up too many explosive passing plays. That matters with the Bengals, Chase and Higgins, and tight end Gesicki coming Monday. Quinn said some coverages that leave the middle of the field exposed may have to be shelved. On offense, he liked Daniels pushing the ball downfield despite two interceptions, and he called Ben Sinnott's game the best he has played in Washington. Injury news: Croskey-Merritt is trending well but no decision has been made on his 21-day window. Lucas Patrick is still in the concussion protocol, and Nick Allegretti drew praise for his pass protection at center. Leo Chenal is back in the building and recovering, but his future is 'too early to call.' Quinn also said he wants more snaps for Kain Medrano behind Sonny Styles and Frankie Luvu, and noted that Deatrich Wise Jr.'s workload depends on how opponents deploy offensively.
